Thoughts on memory:

Anyone who thinks compute will stay in shortage while memory slides into oversupply must be smoking something. Compute and memory are destined to tighten together or deflate together. One cannot die while the other survives.

By the same logic, the pods shorting memory and going long HDD are out of their minds. How do you think HDD isn't joined at the hip with memory? You really think HDD stays safe if this cycle rolls over?

In the end, all of this comes down to nobody having conviction about what happens after 2027. Historically, we have watched P peak one to two quarters before supply ramps, then Q expands and the entire profit pool collapses. But everyone forgets that this cycle runs on nonstandard products, unlike PCs, smartphones, and general purpose servers, and that it was triggered by factors different from past cycles.

This is because of the boomers who still see memory as an industry where you make a killing in the upcycle and lose your shirt in the downcycle. These self proclaimed veterans view memory through the lens of their past experience, and since they drive the market and set the stock prices, memory trades at such a low valuation. What I keep saying is that a sharp collapse like in the past is impossible. A gradual decline is possible. But even if Samsung and SK Hynix margins were cut in half from current levels, they would still trade at a P/E in the teens. That is still roughly half of HDD valuations.

Personally, I think that as memory prices fall, other sources of demand will absorb the supply at each step down. In particular, I expect personal AI demand, led by local AI, to emerge. Looked at another way, for local AI to take off, the hyperscaler driven spike in memory prices has to be brought under control. At current memory prices, local AI can never diversify.

Just as mainframes gave way to PCs and the cloud gave way to smartphones, each time carrying the cycle from P into a Q expansion phase, I think this AI cycle will also move from frontier labs to local open source AI. Based on these historical precedents, I believe local AI will take over the memory cycle from the frontier labs and carry memory demand.

I am not saying memory prices will hold for more than a decade. Memory P will fall at some point. But what is different from the past is that new consumer devices and new consumer demand, such as open source driven local AI, will support the floor for memory.

So the market right now keeps discounting these stocks out of fear of a memory peak nobody can time. This discount is being driven by boomer investors who dismiss the idea that AI supports the downside and keep pushing the view that earnings will collapse and the trough will revert to past levels too. My point is that this is completely wrong.

$CRWV isn’t paying 15% interest. Only 4% of their debt costs that.

I went through the Q2 10-Q line by line. Out of ~$35B in debt, exactly one loan sits at 15%. It’s $1.3B, due March 2028, and already being paid down.

The 15% chart going around is the market yield on their 2032 bond. A higher yield doesn’t change what CoreWeave pays. It works like a mortgage. If you locked in at 3% and rates go to 7%, you’re still paying 3%. CoreWeave locked that bond at 9.625% and still pays 9.625%.

What they actually pay

> $6.6B of convertibles at ~2%
> ~$10B of bonds at 9-10%
> Most secured loans around 9%
> ~8.4% blended across everything

They have roughly $20B of 2026 capex left to fund, and 2027 will need more. Their main funding tool has been loans backed by customer contracts. The investment grade one backed by Meta priced around 5.9% in March. If they keep borrowing that way, I think the math holds.

Gartner says 80% of neocloud providers will stop operating independently by 2030 and I agree.

Sorry but not all of them will be winners, most of them will disappear even if demand is sky high.

If you read my longer takes you know that I think that as a category, neoclouds aren't a great business.

Capex drags on you every quarter, and the only way out is escape velocity: growing faster than your own spending. 

Meaning most will be acquired, merged or starved of capital.

In June Gartner forecasted neoclouds taking 20% of the AI cloud market by 2030. Fewer providers plus a bigger share means the survivors get much, much larger. 

Consolidation is how the winners get made.

So the real question is which one escapes, and here's why I think $NBIS is built differently:

+Customers fund the build. Prepayments covered 50–60% of the capex on its Q2 deals. Most neoclouds borrow against their GPUs, while Nebius gets its customers to pay up front.

+ The margins are already there: about 77% gross margin and a 41% adjusted EBITDA margin in Q2, on revenue up 454% year over year.

+ Pricing keeps rising. GPU prices went up another 17–21% on October 1, and new contracts are signing at $20–25M per MW.

+ It isn't drowning in interest. Last quarter $CRWV paid $640M of interest against $128M of adjusted operating income. Nebius's debt is mostly low-coupon convertibles.

+ The power is locked in. Contracted power has been raised three times this year, to 5 GW.

Gartner's real point is that the industry as a whole won't earn a 12% ROIC until 2032. An industry average tells you how the typical provider does, and I'm not betting on the typical provider. $NBIS is built different.

The risk with Nebius is financing, because the 5 GW build still needs about $250B.

So far they've done a stellar job handling it.

Macro comes and goes, but great companies endure.

$NBIS

I was thinking about what would actually make me sell my NBIS shares. 

Simplified, these are the five things that keep me honest, with how healthy each one looks today (1 = bad / 5= good):

+ Financing gets too expensive (3/5)
 NBIS still has to raise roughly $250B to build out its 5 GW, and only about 20% is secured. If converts and credit get much more expensive, or the market stops taking their paper, growth slows or the share count balloons.

+ Dilution outruns growth (4/5)
 Some dilution is the price of the build-out, and I'm fine with that. What would break the thesis is ARR per share stalling while the share count keeps climbing.

+ Pricing rolls over (5/5)
 The bull case leans on new contracts at $20–25M per MW and GPU prices that are still rising. If contract pricing or on-demand GPU prices start falling, the economics behind every gigawatt shrink.

+ Customers stop paying up front (4/5)
 Prepayments covering 50–60% of capex tell me customers can't find this capacity elsewhere. If those shrink, demand is cooling.

+ Power slips (3/5)
 Contracted power that doesn't come online on time is revenue that doesn't show up, and power is the slowest input in the whole stack.

Demand is the easy part right now. 

The weakest scores are on financing and delivery, and that's where I'll be watching.

Healthcare:
- healthcare is the largest category on this list. It is literally the future. Huge aging population

- home health aides, therapy assistants, and health services managers are scaling to support aging-in-place and higher-acuity outpatient care

Technology:
- data volume is compounding across every industry (including healthcare records, imaging, and claims)
- data scientists exist to turn that volume into usable signals
- AI requires continuous research, not just implementation.
- computer and information research scientists invent the next algorithms and systems as basic data science becomes more widespread
- connectivity permanently expands the attack surface - Information security analysts grow because the cost of being unsecured keeps rising; especially in healthcare, finance, and critical infrastructure
- stocks for AI infrastructure & platforms: $NVDA, $MSFT, $GOOGL, $AMZN, $AVGO, $AMD, $SNOW, $PLTR
- stocks for cybersecurity: $CRWD, $PANW, $ZS, $FTNT, $S, $OKTA

Renewables:
- solar and wind appear because of the energy transition, but the absolute job numbers remain small compared with healthcare and tech.
- solar photovoltaic installers and wind turbine technicians are high-percentage growth roles tied to new capacity and maintenance.
- these stocks remain more policy-sensitive and cyclical than the healthcare or cybersecurity names.

- industrial machinery mechanics is the main non-service name on the list.

Okay so what to do?
In my opinion, healthcare is the biggest and most durable demand engine on this list. An aging population, doctor shortages, and the move toward more care at home and outside hospitals are already locked in. This is the part of the market that should act as the ballast in a portfolio. Have some real exposure to healthcare.

Tech (data, AI, and cybersecurity) is the higher-upside layer sitting on top of that. These names tend to move more when the market is in growth mode, but they also carry more volatility. So make sure you have exposure here in tech as well for the next decade to outperform the markets.  

Renewables and industrial machinery show up on the list, but they are smaller pieces of the overall picture and more sensitive to policy and the economic cycle. It's okay to have crazy volatile names, but make sure you size it correctly.

【美股复盘 · 10月15日】

**【大市】**
美股周四(15日)表现分化,指数升跌不一,资金明显由AI基建硬件一端撤出,转入软件及投机性成长股。道指(DIA)收报521.18,升1.08%;罗素小型股(IWM)收报275.05,升1.36%,升幅居各主要指数之首;标普(SPY)收报771.79,升0.28%,全日靠稳;惟纳指(QQQ)反复偏软,收报728.00,跌0.13%,为唯一收低的主要指数。市宽呈拉锯格局,104只观察股中53只上升、51只下跌,升跌比近乎对半,显示大市升幅并非来自普涨,而是来自板块之间的位置转移。

**【板块】**
软件股造好, $CRM ADBE 同升4.57%, APP 升6.52%;加密货币相关股领先大市, CRCL 急升9.33%, COIN 升6.32%;量子计算概念全线走强, IONQ 升9.33%、 RGTI 升8.13%、 QBTS 升6.53%。沽压则高度集中在AI硬件链:服务器及企业硬件重挫, HPE 急泻7.10%, DELL 跌6.80%;网络设备 ANET 挫5.04%、 CSCO 跌3.34%;电源散热 VRT 跌3.63%;光通讯 COHR 跌4.83%;半导体设备 AMAT 跌3.72%、 AEHR 跌3.19%;模拟及混合信号芯片 SMTC 暴泻10.01%,为全日最弱。航天股分化, ASTS 升5.51%,惟 RKLB 跌6.64%。

**【焦点】**
全日最值得注意的一组背驰,是算力租赁与算力硬件的分道: CRWV 逆市升5.94%,而为其供货的服务器、网络与光模块一方几乎全线失守,反映沽压针对的是硬件供应端的订单与毛利预期,而非AI用量本身。题材方面,美光台湾厂劳资争议已升级至台当局公开介入、促劳资「真诚协商」,其DRAM主力产能位于台中而非美国,存储供应的扰动风险成为设备与存储链情绪的压制项;另一端,苹果智能在中国获批、月底上beta,惟仅15 Pro以后机型可运行,市场更倾向视之为换机周期而非即期软件收入;Meta与苹果将开源权重模型引入Mac本地运行,则将叙事重心由数据中心外设移向终端内存与软件层。

**【小结】**
市场的减磅并未外溢至整体风险偏好——小型股与道指同步造好,升跌家数接近对半,属典型的链内轮动而非系统性去风险。技术上,纳指(QQQ)全日收在728关附近,为四大指数中唯一未能收复失地的一只;标普(SPY)771至772区间与罗素(IWM)275关成为短线观察位。分析指,在AI硬件链的毛利疑虑消化完毕之前,指数层面的强弱将继续由软件与硬件之间的资金配置决定,而非由单一宏观变量主导。
